# THE CONVERSATION setup-git HAS WITH A STUDENT, as a table, in one place.
#
# WHY A FILE RATHER THAN A KEYSTROKE STRING AT EACH CALL SITE. 35-setup-git-shim.sh drives
# setup-git 38 times, and 26 of those runs are the same conversation with one thing changed. As
# `|`-separated keystrokes that sequence was written out 39 times, so a screen added or removed --
# which issues #53, #58 and #92 each did -- was a 39-site edit whose failures arrived as
# assertions about something else entirely, at whatever site noticed first. Here it is one edit.
#
# EVERY STEP NAMES THE SCREEN IT ANSWERS, BY CATALOGUE KEY. The harness resolves the key to its
# prose, so nothing here hardcodes wording -- the same rule assert_says_key exists for. A step is
# not sent until that prose is on the screen AND the terminal is in the state that read implies,
# so a reflowed flow fails ONCE, by name, at the step that diverged, instead of typing the right
# number of keys into the wrong prompts.
#
#   line KEY...   -> type TEXT      a prompt read with `read -r`: canonical, the terminal echoing
#   secret KEY... -> paste TEXT     read_secret: `stty -echo -icanon`, tallied, never echoed
#   menu  KEY...  -> pick KEY       an arrow-key menu, whose KEYS ARE ITS OPTIONS IN ORDER
#   include FLOW                    another flow, spliced in here
#   optional                        everything after it in this flow may go unreached
#
# `pick` NAMES THE OPTION AND THE HARNESS COUNTS THE ARROWS. That is the half that makes a
# reordered menu a one-line change rather than a hunt for `\033[B\033[B\n` at seven call sites --
# and it puts in the file what the comment this change deletes had to say in prose:
# "down, down, Enter -- the third option, I'm stuck".
#
# {{ID}}, {{NAME}} and {{TOKEN}} are filled in by the caller. THE TOKEN NEVER PASSES THROUGH awk:
# the expansion below leaves the placeholder alone and lib/setup-git-shim.sh substitutes it in the
# shell, so it reaches no argv and no environment on its way to the pty. See files/setup-git:680-683.

# ─── the pieces ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[[identity]]
line    prompt.sunetid                                  -> type {{ID}}
menu    opt.correct opt.retype                          -> pick opt.correct
line    prompt.name                                     -> type {{NAME}}
menu    opt.correct opt.retype                          -> pick opt.correct

[[checkpoint-ok]]
menu    opt.all-done opt.need-help                      -> pick opt.all-done

[[checkpoint-help]]
menu    opt.all-done opt.need-help                      -> pick opt.need-help

# The link screen and the paste behind it. Both ways through the #58 menu are here, so the one
# that is not the default is exercised by naming it rather than by counting arrows.
[[get-token]]
menu    opt.have-token opt.by-hand                      -> pick opt.have-token
secret  prompt.token                                    -> paste {{TOKEN}}

[[get-token-by-hand]]
menu    opt.have-token opt.by-hand                      -> pick opt.by-hand
secret  prompt.token                                    -> paste {{TOKEN}}

[[account-ok]]
menu    opt.thats-me opt.not-my-account                 -> pick opt.thats-me

[[account-wrong]]
menu    opt.thats-me opt.not-my-account                 -> pick opt.not-my-account

# ─── the whole clean first run ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

[[happy]]
include identity
include checkpoint-ok
include get-token
include account-ok

[[happy-by-hand]]
include identity
include checkpoint-ok
include get-token-by-hand
include account-ok

# EVERYTHING UP TO THE PASTE AND NO FURTHER, which is the run a failing `git config` produces:
# apply_config gives up before whoami_login, so the account confirmation is never drawn. As a
# keystroke string that was an eighth key nobody consumed and nothing recorded.
[[happy-to-token]]
include identity
include checkpoint-ok
include get-token

# ─── the three ways out of a failed probe ──────────────────────────────────────

[[retry-probes]]
menu    opt.followed-instructions opt.reenter-token opt.stuck  -> pick opt.followed-instructions

[[reenter-token]]
menu    opt.followed-instructions opt.reenter-token opt.stuck  -> pick opt.reenter-token
include get-token
include account-ok

[[stuck]]
menu    opt.followed-instructions opt.reenter-token opt.stuck  -> pick opt.stuck

# The same, for a run that may or may not reach it: 90-setup-git-github.sh runs against the real
# GitHub, where the point is to find out WHETHER a probe fails.
[[stuck-if-a-probe-failed]]
optional
menu    opt.followed-instructions opt.reenter-token opt.stuck  -> pick opt.stuck

# ─── the second run ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[[second-run-check]]
menu    opt.just-check opt.start-over opt.quit          -> pick opt.just-check

[[second-run-start-over]]
menu    opt.just-check opt.start-over opt.quit          -> pick opt.start-over

[[second-run-quit]]
menu    opt.just-check opt.start-over opt.quit          -> pick opt.quit

# ─── validation, as the student meets it ───────────────────────────────────────
# EACH REJECTION IS A STEP, AND IT NAMES THE COMPLAINT IT EXPECTS. That is what replaces
# `grep -o '3 to 8 letters and numbers' | grep -c .`: the count used to be an occurrence count
# rather than a row count, because the row break between two complaints was the terminal echoing
# a keystroke and sg_feed raced it (35-setup-git-shim.sh:476-509). Here the complaint is verified
# where it happened, in order, by key, and there is nothing left to race.

[[bad-sunetids]]
line    prompt.sunetid                                  -> type jane.doe
line    err.sunetid-invalid prompt.retry                -> type ab
line    err.sunetid-invalid prompt.retry                -> type me@cs.stanford.edu
line    err.sunetid-is-an-email prompt.retry            -> type "   JDoe   "
menu    opt.correct opt.retype                          -> pick opt.correct
line    prompt.name                                     -> type {{NAME}}
menu    opt.correct opt.retype                          -> pick opt.correct

# A structurally valid SUNetID that is somebody else's: nothing but the confirmation can catch it.
[[retype-sunetid]]
line    prompt.sunetid                                  -> type wrong
menu    opt.correct opt.retype                          -> pick opt.retype
include identity

[[classic-token]]
menu    opt.have-token opt.by-hand                      -> pick opt.have-token
secret  prompt.token                                    -> paste ghp_16C7e42F292c6912E7710c838347Ae178B4a
secret  err.token-classic prompt.retry                  -> paste {{TOKEN}}

[[junk-token]]
menu    opt.have-token opt.by-hand                      -> pick opt.have-token
secret  prompt.token                                    -> paste hello
secret  err.token-shape prompt.retry                    -> paste {{TOKEN}}

[[partial-token]]
menu    opt.have-token opt.by-hand                      -> pick opt.have-token
secret  prompt.token                                    -> paste {{HALF}}
secret  err.token-partial prompt.retry                  -> paste {{TOKEN}}
